namespace guetzli {

enum JPEGReadError {
  JPEG_OK = 0,
  JPEG_SOI_NOT_FOUND,
  JPEG_SOF_NOT_FOUND,
  JPEG_UNEXPECTED_EOF,
  JPEG_MARKER_BYTE_NOT_FOUND,
  JPEG_UNSUPPORTED_MARKER,
  JPEG_WRONG_MARKER_SIZE,
  JPEG_INVALID_PRECISION,
  JPEG_INVALID_WIDTH,
  JPEG_INVALID_HEIGHT,
  JPEG_INVALID_NUMCOMP,
  JPEG_INVALID_SAMP_FACTOR,
  JPEG_INVALID_START_OF_SCAN,
  JPEG_INVALID_END_OF_SCAN,
  JPEG_INVALID_SCAN_BIT_POSITION,
  JPEG_INVALID_COMPS_IN_SCAN,
  JPEG_INVALID_HUFFMAN_INDEX,
  JPEG_INVALID_QUANT_TBL_INDEX,
  JPEG_INVALID_QUANT_VAL,
  JPEG_INVALID_MARKER_LEN,
  JPEG_INVALID_SAMPLING_FACTORS,
  JPEG_INVALID_HUFFMAN_CODE,
  JPEG_INVALID_SYMBOL,
  JPEG_NON_REPRESENTABLE_DC_COEFF,
  JPEG_NON_REPRESENTABLE_AC_COEFF,
  JPEG_INVALID_SCAN,
  JPEG_OVERLAPPING_SCANS,
  JPEG_INVALID_SCAN_ORDER,
  JPEG_EXTRA_ZERO_RUN,
  JPEG_DUPLICATE_DRI,
  JPEG_DUPLICATE_SOF,
  JPEG_WRONG_RESTART_MARKER,
  JPEG_DUPLICATE_COMPONENT_ID,
  JPEG_COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND,
  JPEG_HUFFMAN_TABLE_NOT_FOUND,
  JPEG_HUFFMAN_TABLE_ERROR,
  JPEG_QUANT_TABLE_NOT_FOUND,
  JPEG_EMPTY_DHT,
  JPEG_EMPTY_DQT,
  JPEG_OUT_OF_BAND_COEFF,
  JPEG_EOB_RUN_TOO_LONG,
  JPEG_IMAGE_TOO_LARGE,
};

}  // namespace guetzli
objects.description: Enumeration of error/status codes returned by JPEG parsing routines within the guetzli namespace. Values cover success (JPEG_OK) and a wide range of structural, range, and consistency errors encountered while reading JPEG streams. No additional lifecycle management is required for enum values.

Abstract interface for comparing an output image against a baseline image in the Guetzli encoder. It encapsulates metric computation, per-block comparison, acceptance testing, and distance-map reporting. This header defines only the interface; concrete implementations are defined elsewhere.

Configuration struct for the Guetzli processing pipeline. Holds encoding/quality knobs like target Butteraugli distance, metadata handling, chroma subsampling preferences, and model/zeroing behavior. Default member initializers provide typical defaults.
Result container for Guetzli processing when operating on JPEGData. Contains the produced JPEG bitstream (jpeg_data) and an associated quality/score metric.

A simple statistics and debugging data holder used by the guetzli namespace. It tracks integer counters by name, optional debug output destinations (either a std::string buffer or a FILE*), and the associated input/output filename. Default constructor leaves all members default-initialized; debug_output and debug_output_file are null by default. Lifetime and ownership of debug_output and debug_output_file are external; this struct does not manage or close them.

functions.name: guetzli::JPEGData::Is420
functions.signature: bool guetzli::JPEGData::Is420() const
functions.description: Returns whether the JPEGData instance represents 4:2:0 chroma subsampling (YUV 4:2:0). Intended to be called after JPEGData has been populated (e.g., by a parser or initializer) to query its sampling layout. Exact criteria are not documented here, but typically depends on component sampling factors relative to max_h_samp_factor and max_v_samp_factor. Details of the internal check are unknown from this header.
requirements: The JPEGData object must be in a valid, initialized state (e.g., sampling factors and components set) before calling. (Inferred from purpose)
No other explicit requirements are stated in the header.

functions.name: guetzli::JPEGData::Is444
functions.signature: bool guetzli::JPEGData::Is444() const
functions.description: Returns whether the JPEGData instance represents 4:4:4 chroma sampling (no subsampling). Intended to be used after JPEGData has been populated to query if all components use full resolution. Exact internal criteria are not documented here; typically checks per-component sampling factors against the maximums. Details of the internal check are unknown from this header.
requirements: The JPEGData object should have valid component and sampling-factor metadata initialized before calling. (Inferred from purpose)
No other explicit requirements are stated in the header.

functions.name: guetzli::InitJPEGDataForYUV444
functions.signature: void guetzli::InitJPEGDataForYUV444(int w, int h, guetzli::JPEGData* jpg)
functions.description: Initializes a JPEGData structure to represent an image laid out for YUV 4:4:4 sampling with the given width and height. Typically used to set up component lists, sampling factors, block dimensions, and related fields for a 4:4:4 JPEG before filling in coefficients and tables. Exact fields modified are not documented in this header; details are inferred from the name.
requirements: jpg must be a non-null pointer to a writable JPEGData instance. (Inferred from pointer parameter)
w and h should be valid image dimensions; typically positive integers greater than zero. (Inferred from common image dimension requirements)
Any pre-existing contents of *jpg may be overwritten or reset by initialization. Behavior on pre-populated structures is not documented.

functions.name: guetzli::SaveQuantTables
functions.signature: void guetzli::SaveQuantTables(const int q[3][64], guetzli::JPEGData* jpg)
functions.description: Stores (saves) up to three 8x8 quantization tables into the provided JPEGData object. The input is a 3x64 array (three tables, each with 64 entries in natural block order). Intended to be called when preparing or modifying JPEGData prior to encoding or further processing. Specific handling of precision, table indices, and existing tables is not documented in this header.
requirements: q must point to a valid array of shape [3][64] containing 64 coefficients per table. (Inferred from the parameter type and kDCTBlockSize)
jpg must be a non-null pointer to a writable JPEGData instance. (Inferred from pointer parameter)
Value ranges and interpretation of q entries (e.g., allowed coefficient ranges or precision) are not specified in this header and thus are unknown.

functions.name: guetzli::AddApp0Data
functions.signature: void guetzli::AddApp0Data(JPEGData* jpg);
functions.description: Adds an APP0 (JFIF) header segment to the provided JPEGData structure. Intended to be called while constructing or finalizing a JPEG bitstream representation in memory.
requirements: jpg must be a valid, non-null pointer to a JPEGData object that the function can modify.
The JPEGData object should be initialized/allocated prior to the call (inferred from pointer usage).
Caller should ensure the JPEGData is in a state where adding an APP0 segment is appropriate for the intended output (e.g., not already containing conflicting APP0 data; not stated in the header).

functions.name: guetzli::EncodeRGBToJpeg
functions.signature: bool guetzli::EncodeRGBToJpeg(const std::vector<uint8_t>& rgb, int w, int h, JPEGData* jpg);
functions.description: Encodes raw interleaved RGB pixel data into a JPEG representation stored in jpg. Returns true on success, false on failure. This overload uses internally chosen/default quantization tables.
requirements: rgb provides the source pixel data; its size should correspond to w * h * 3 bytes for 8-bit RGB (inferred from parameter types and conventional usage; not explicitly stated).
w must be the image width in pixels (non-negative/positive expected; not explicitly stated).
h must be the image height in pixels (non-negative/positive expected; not explicitly stated).
jpg must be a valid, non-null pointer to a JPEGData object where the encoded JPEG will be written.
Caller must check the boolean return value to handle encoding failures.

functions.name: guetzli::WriteJpeg
functions.signature: bool WriteJpeg(const JPEGData& jpg, bool strip_metadata, JPEGOutput out);
functions.description: Serializes a JPEGData structure into a JPEG byte stream and writes it using the provided JPEGOutput callback. Use this to emit a complete JPEG file/stream, optionally stripping metadata markers when strip_metadata is true.
requirements: jpg must be a valid, fully-initialized JPEGData object per guetzli/jpeg_data.h.
out must contain a valid callback (JPEGOutputHook) that can accept the bytes written; the callback must return the exact number of bytes written or -1 on error.
The output callback must be prepared to be called multiple times and may be called with len == 0.
If strip_metadata is true, the resulting stream will exclude metadata; callers relying on metadata should pass false.
Caller should check the boolean return value; false indicates a write or serialization error.

functions.name: guetzli::BuildSequentialHuffmanCodes
functions.signature: void BuildSequentialHuffmanCodes(const JPEGData& jpg, std::vector<HuffmanCodeTable>* dc_huffman_code_tables, std::vector<HuffmanCodeTable>* ac_huffman_code_tables);
functions.description: Constructs Huffman code tables for sequential JPEG scans based on the content/layout of the given JPEGData. Populates/overwrites the DC and AC Huffman code tables vectors with code depths and codes suitable for writing the image.
requirements: dc_huffman_code_tables must be non-null.
ac_huffman_code_tables must be non-null.
jpg must describe components/scans consistently so that Huffman tables can be derived.
The provided vectors may be resized or overwritten by the function; caller should not rely on their prior contents after the call.

functions.name: guetzli::BuildDCHistograms
functions.signature: void BuildDCHistograms(const JPEGData& jpg, JpegHistogram* histo);
functions.description: Accumulates symbol counts for DC coefficients across the JPEGData into a JpegHistogram. Intended for building entropy coding statistics prior to constructing DC Huffman tables.
requirements: histo must be non-null and refer to a valid JpegHistogram to receive counts.
Caller should ensure histo is cleared/reset if previous contents should not influence the results.
jpg must contain valid DC coefficient data.

functions.name: guetzli::BuildACHistograms
functions.signature: void BuildACHistograms(const JPEGData& jpg, JpegHistogram* histo);
functions.description: Accumulates symbol counts for AC coefficients across the JPEGData into a JpegHistogram. Intended for building entropy coding statistics prior to constructing AC Huffman tables.
requirements: histo must be non-null and refer to a valid JpegHistogram to receive counts.
Caller should ensure histo is cleared/reset if previous contents should not influence the results.
jpg must contain valid AC coefficient data.

functions.name: guetzli::JpegHeaderSize
functions.signature: size_t JpegHeaderSize(const JPEGData& jpg, bool strip_metadata);
functions.description: Estimates or computes the byte size of the JPEG header (markers/tables/metadata prior to scan data) for the given JPEGData, optionally excluding metadata when strip_metadata is true.
requirements: jpg must be a valid JPEGData describing header-related structures (quant tables, Huffman tables, frame/scan headers, etc.).
Interpretation of strip_metadata matches how WriteJpeg handles metadata; pass the same value if coordinating size and write operations.

functions.name: guetzli::EstimateJpegDataSize
functions.signature: size_t EstimateJpegDataSize(const int num_components, const std::vector<JpegHistogram>& histograms);
functions.description: Returns an estimated size in bytes for the entropy-coded JPEG data given the number of components and their histograms. Useful for preallocation or size prediction before writing scans.
requirements: num_components should be a non-negative integer; typically corresponds to the number of image components (e.g., 1 for gray, 3 for YCbCr).
histograms must contain histogram data relevant to the components/scans to be encoded.
The mapping between num_components and histograms is not specified here; callers must ensure consistency with the encoder’s expectations (unknown details).

functions.name: guetzli::HistogramEntropyCost
functions.signature: size_t HistogramEntropyCost(const JpegHistogram& histo, const uint8_t depths[256]);
functions.description: Computes the entropy coding cost (in bytes or bits-equivalent) for a histogram given a fixed Huffman code depth table. Intended to evaluate coding efficiency for a particular set of Huffman depths.
requirements: depths must reference an array of exactly 256 uint8_t entries.
histo must contain valid counts (e.g., initialized via JpegHistogram::Clear/Add).

functions.name: guetzli::HistogramHeaderCost
functions.signature: size_t HistogramHeaderCost(const JpegHistogram& histo);
functions.description: Computes the header cost of encoding a Huffman table that would represent the given histogram (e.g., the bits/bytes needed to transmit the table).
requirements: histo must contain valid counts representative of the symbols to be encoded.

functions.name: guetzli::UpdateACHistogramForDCTBlock
functions.signature: void UpdateACHistogramForDCTBlock(const coeff_t* coeffs, JpegHistogram* ac_histogram);
functions.description: Updates an AC coefficient histogram with the contribution from a single DCT block of JPEG coefficients pointed to by coeffs. Use this when incrementally building AC histograms per block.
requirements: coeffs must be a non-null pointer to a valid block of JPEG AC coefficients as defined by coeff_t in guetzli/jpeg_data.h (exact required length is not specified here; typically a full 8x8 block).
ac_histogram must be non-null and refer to a valid JpegHistogram to be updated.
Caller should ensure ac_histogram is initialized/cleared as appropriate before accumulation.

functions.name: guetzli::ClusterHistograms
functions.signature: size_t ClusterHistograms(JpegHistogram* histo, size_t* num, int* histo_indexes, uint8_t* depths);
functions.description: Clusters multiple histograms to reduce the number of distinct Huffman tables, returning a measure related to the resulting cost or number of clusters. Also outputs mapping/indexing and depth information through the provided buffers.
requirements: histo must be non-null and point to an array of JpegHistogram elements; exact required length and layout are unspecified here (depends on *num).
num must be non-null; on input it likely specifies the number of histograms; on output it may be updated to the number of clusters (exact behavior unknown from header).
histo_indexes must be non-null and point to an array large enough to receive per-histogram cluster indexes (exact size unspecified).
depths must be non-null and point to a buffer large enough for generated depth data (exact size unspecified).

Callers must ensure buffer sizes and the value pointed to by num are consistent with the implementation’s expectations; details are not available in this header and must be confirmed against the source.

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::Compare
functions.signature: virtual void guetzli::Comparator::Compare(const guetzli::OutputImage& img) = 0;
functions.description: Compares the provided image against the internal baseline image and stores the resulting distance map inside the comparator for later queries (e.g., distmap, distmap_aggregate, ScoreOutputSize, DistanceOK). Intended to be called whenever you have a candidate output image to evaluate.
requirements: img must have the same width and height as the baseline image.
The comparator instance must have a defined baseline image (implementation-specific; usually supplied at construction).
Subsequent queries like distmap(), distmap_aggregate(), ScoreOutputSize(), and DistanceOK() refer to the results of the most recent Compare() call, or the baseline if Compare() hasn’t been called.

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::StartBlockComparisons
functions.signature: virtual void guetzli::Comparator::StartBlockComparisons() = 0;
functions.description: Marks the beginning of a sequence of per-block comparisons, enabling subsequent CompareBlock calls.
requirements: Must be called before any CompareBlock() call.
Should be paired with a later FinishBlockComparisons() call to end the block-comparison phase.

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::FinishBlockComparisons
functions.signature: virtual void guetzli::Comparator::FinishBlockComparisons() = 0;
functions.description: Marks the end of a sequence of per-block comparisons, after which CompareBlock can no longer be called.
requirements: Must be called after StartBlockComparisons() when finished with all CompareBlock() calls.
After this call, no further CompareBlock() calls are allowed until a new StartBlockComparisons().

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::SwitchBlock
functions.signature: virtual void guetzli::Comparator::SwitchBlock(int block_x, int block_y, int factor_x, int factor_y) = 0;
functions.description: Sets the coordinates of the current macro-block (and scaling factors) used to interpret subsequent CompareBlock calls.
requirements: Should be called after StartBlockComparisons() and before CompareBlock() for blocks within the specified macro-block.
block_x and block_y specify the macro-block position; factor_x and factor_y specify macro-block scaling/stride (exact semantics are implementation-specific/unknown).
Callers must ensure chosen coordinates correspond to valid macro-blocks within the image (bounds are implementation-specific/unknown).

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::CompareBlock
functions.signature: virtual double guetzli::Comparator::CompareBlock(const guetzli::OutputImage& img, int off_x, int off_y) const = 0;
functions.description: Compares the 8x8 block at offsets (off_x, off_y) within the current macro-block of the baseline image with the same block of the given image, returning the per-block distance (metric depends on the comparator).
requirements: StartBlockComparisons() must have been called prior to any CompareBlock().
A valid SwitchBlock() must have been set to define the current macro-block before calling CompareBlock() for that macro-block.
FinishBlockComparisons() must not have been called yet when invoking CompareBlock().
img must have the same dimensions as the baseline image.
off_x and off_y must identify an 8x8 block inside the current macro-block (valid range and macro-block size are implementation-specific/unknown).

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::ScoreOutputSize
functions.signature: virtual double guetzli::Comparator::ScoreOutputSize(int size) const = 0;
functions.description: Computes a combined score for the last compared image (or the baseline if Compare was never called), taking into account the provided output size and the similarity metric maintained by the comparator.
requirements: size represents the output size (typically in bytes) and should be non-negative.
The score is defined relative to the last Compare() call’s result, or the baseline if Compare() hasn’t been called.

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::DistanceOK
functions.signature: virtual bool guetzli::Comparator::DistanceOK(double target_mul) const = 0;
functions.description: Returns whether the last compared image (or the baseline if Compare wasn’t called) satisfies the comparator’s acceptance criteria. target_mul scales the criteria: 1.0 uses default, <1.0 stricter, >1.0 looser.
requirements: target_mul adjusts the acceptance criteria as documented: 1.0 original, <1.0 more strict, >1.0 less strict. No explicit bounds beyond that are specified.
Result refers to the last Compare() call or the baseline if none was made.

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::distmap
functions.signature: virtual const std::vector<float> guetzli::Comparator::distmap() const = 0;
functions.description: Returns the distance map between the baseline image and the image used in the last Compare() call (or the baseline image if Compare() was not called). The map dimensions match the baseline image; interpretation of values is comparator-dependent.
requirements: May be called before or after Compare(); if Compare() hasn’t been called, returns the baseline-vs-baseline map as defined by the implementation.
The returned vector corresponds in size to the baseline image dimensions (exact layout is implementation-specific).

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::distmap_aggregate
functions.signature: virtual float guetzli::Comparator::distmap_aggregate() const = 0;
functions.description: Returns an aggregate distance/similarity value summarizing the distance map of the last Compare() call (or the baseline if Compare() wasn’t called). Interpretation is comparator-dependent.
requirements: May be called without a prior Compare(); behavior refers to the baseline in that case.
Exact range/units of the aggregate are implementation-specific/unknown.

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::BlockErrorLimit
functions.signature: virtual float guetzli::Comparator::BlockErrorLimit() const = 0;
functions.description: Returns a heuristic cutoff on per-block errors; distortions with block error above this value are not considered by the comparator’s search heuristics.
requirements: No inputs; interpretation and range of the returned limit are comparator-dependent/unknown.

functions.name: guetzli::Comparator::ComputeBlockErrorAdjustmentWeights
functions.signature: virtual void guetzli::Comparator::ComputeBlockErrorAdjustmentWeights(int direction, int max_block_dist, double target_mul, int factor_x, int factor_y, const std::vector<float>& distmap, std::vector<float>* block_weight) = 0;
functions.description: Fills block_weight with relative per-block error adjustment weights derived from the provided distance map and a search direction. The result guides how block errors should be adjusted during search. Semantically static; it does not depend on the last Compare() call. target_mul has the same acceptance-tuning semantics as in DistanceOK.
requirements: direction must indicate search direction: +1 for upwards, -1 for downwards.
distmap is the current distance map used as input; its dimensions/layout should match the image/block grid expected by the comparator (implementation-specific).

block_weight must be a valid non-null pointer; the function will fill the image of weights corresponding to the provided distmap (may resize as needed; resizing behavior is implementation-specific/unknown).
factor_x and factor_y must be valid scaling/block factors consistent with the block grid used elsewhere (exact constraints are implementation-specific/unknown).
max_block_dist should represent a limit/scale for block distances (exact meaning and valid range are implementation-specific/unknown).
target_mul follows DistanceOK semantics: 1.0 original criteria, <1.0 stricter, >1.0 looser.

functions.name: guetzli::Process
functions.signature: bool guetzli::Process(const guetzli::Params& params, guetzli::ProcessStats* stats, const std::string& in_data, std::string* out_data)
functions.description: Optimize/encode a JPEG from an input byte string. On success returns true and writes the resulting JPEG bitstream to *out_data. Intended for cases where the input is a pre-existing JPEG bitstream provided as a std::string.
requirements: out_data must be a valid, non-null pointer.
stats must be a valid, non-null pointer if statistics collection is desired; behavior is unknown if null.
in_data should contain the input image data; based on naming and library patterns this overload expects a JPEG bitstream.
On success (return true) the function writes a JPEG-encoded result to *out_data; callers should clear or replace any existing contents as needed.
Callers should check the returned bool for success before using *out_data.

functions.name: guetzli::ProcessJpegData
functions.signature: bool guetzli::ProcessJpegData(const guetzli::Params& params, const guetzli::JPEGData& jpg_in, guetzli::Comparator* comparator, guetzli::GuetzliOutput* out, guetzli::ProcessStats* stats)
functions.description: Optimize/encode from a parsed JPEG (JPEGData) using a provided Comparator. On success returns true and fills *out with the resulting JPEG bitstream (and score). Intended for advanced usage where the caller supplies decoded JPEG structure and a perceptual comparator.
requirements: comparator must be a valid, non-null pointer to a Comparator instance prepared for the image being processed.
out must be a valid, non-null pointer; on success it will be populated (e.g., jpeg_data and score).
stats must be a valid, non-null pointer if statistics are needed; behavior is unknown if null.
jpg_in must represent a valid/initialized JPEGData structure consistent with the expected image content.
Callers must check the returned bool for success before using data written to *out.

data_types.description: A byte buffer containing raw, interleaved 8-bit RGB pixel data with no header or metadata. Expected size is exactly width * height * 3 bytes, with bytes ordered as R, G, B for each pixel in row-major order.
A bytestream representing a JPEG file/stream, typically beginning with the SOI marker 0xFF 0xD8 and containing valid JPEG markers and entropy-coded image data. May include metadata segments.
An unconstrained byte string used as general text or keys in maps. No specific encoding or structure is required; may contain any bytes and is often truncated to a small length.
Bytes read from a fuzz-generated file path. The filename itself is not important; the file’s contents are treated as arbitrary text/bytes without required structure.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple, Dict

# This script generates compact, valid baseline JPEG bitstreams suitable for
# seeding guetzli::Process fuzzing. It constructs a minimal JFIF JPEG with
# standard Huffman/quant tables and entropy data consisting of zero blocks.

MARK = {
    'SOI': b"\xFF\xD8",
    'EOI': b"\xFF\xD9",
    'APP0': 0xE0,
    'DQT': 0xDB,
    'SOF0': 0xC0,
    'DHT': 0xC4,
    'SOS': 0xDA,
}

def be16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>H', n)

def segment(marker: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\xFF" + bytes([marker]) + be16(len(payload) + 2) + payload

def make_app0_jfif(x_density: int = 72, y_density: int = 72) -> bytes:
    ident = b"JFIF\x00"
    ver = bytes([1, 2])
    units = 1  # dpi
    xden = be16(max(1, x_density))
    yden = be16(max(1, y_density))
    thumb_w = 0
    thumb_h = 0
    payload = ident + ver + bytes([units]) + xden + yden + bytes([thumb_w, thumb_h])
    return segment(MARK['APP0'], payload)

def make_dqt(qt: List[int], table_id: int) -> bytes:
    hdr = bytes([(0 << 4) | (table_id & 0x0F)])
    body = bytes(qt[:64])
    return segment(MARK['DQT'], hdr + body)

def make_sof0(width: int, height: int, samp_420: bool) -> bytes:
    p = 8
    y = max(1, height)
    x = max(1, width)
    nf = 3
    parts = [bytes([p]) + be16(y) + be16(x) + bytes([nf])]
    if samp_420:
        parts.append(bytes([1, 0x22, 0]))  # Y, H=2 V=2, Tq=0
        parts.append(bytes([2, 0x11, 1]))  # Cb, H=1 V=1, Tq=1
        parts.append(bytes([3, 0x11, 1]))  # Cr, H=1 V=1, Tq=1
    else:
        parts.append(bytes([1, 0x11, 0]))
        parts.append(bytes([2, 0x11, 1]))
        parts.append(bytes([3, 0x11, 1]))
    return segment(MARK['SOF0'], b''.join(parts))

def make_dht(bits: List[int], vals: List[int], tc: int, th: int) -> bytes:
    hdr = bytes([(tc << 4) | (th & 0x0F)])
    li = bytes(bits[:16])
    hv = bytes(vals)
    return segment(MARK['DHT'], hdr + li + hv)

def make_sos() -> bytes:
    ns = 3
    hdr = [bytes([ns])]
    hdr.append(bytes([1, 0x00]))  # Y uses DC0/AC0
    hdr.append(bytes([2, 0x11]))  # Cb uses DC1/AC1
    hdr.append(bytes([3, 0x11]))  # Cr uses DC1/AC1
    hdr.append(bytes([0, 63, 0]))
    return segment(MARK['SOS'], b''.join(hdr))

class BitWriter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.buf = bytearray()
        self.acc = 0
        self.nbits = 0
    def write_bits(self, code: int, length: int):
        for i in range(length - 1, -1, -1):
            bit = (code >> i) & 1
            self.acc = (self.acc << 1) | bit
            self.nbits += 1
            if self.nbits == 8:
                b = self.acc & 0xFF
                self.buf.append(b)
                if b == 0xFF:
                    self.buf.append(0x00)
                self.acc = 0
                self.nbits = 0
    def byte_align(self):
        if self.nbits != 0:
            self.write_bits(0, 8 - self.nbits)
    def get(self) -> bytes:
        return bytes(self.buf)

def build_huff_codes(bits: List[int], vals: List[int]) -> Dict[int, Tuple[int,int]]:
    # Validate inputs to avoid index errors
    if len(bits) < 16:
        raise ValueError("bits must have length >= 16")
    total = sum(bits[:16])
    if total > len(vals):
        # Pad vals with zeros to the required length; symbols themselves don't matter for our usage
        vals = list(vals) + [0] * (total - len(vals))
    codes: Dict[int, Tuple[int,int]] = {}
    code = 0
    k = 0
    for l in range(1, 17):
        cnt = bits[l - 1]
        for _ in range(cnt):
            sym = vals[k]
            codes[sym] = (code, l)
            code += 1
            k += 1
        code <<= 1
    return codes

def emit_zero_block(bw: BitWriter, dc_codes: Dict[int, Tuple[int,int]], ac_codes: Dict[int, Tuple[int,int]]):
    code, length = dc_codes[DC0]
    bw.write_bits(code, length)
    eob_code, eob_len = ac_codes[EOB]
    bw.write_bits(eob_code, eob_len)


def make_entropy_data(width: int, height: int, samp_420: bool) -> bytes:
    if samp_420:
        mcu_w, mcu_h = 16, 16
        y_blocks = 4
    else:
        mcu_w, mcu_h = 8, 8
        y_blocks = 1
    mcus_x = (width + mcu_w - 1) // mcu_w
    mcus_y = (height + mcu_h - 1) // mcu_h

    bw = BitWriter()
    for _ in range(mcus_y * mcus_x):
        for _ in range(y_blocks):
            emit_zero_block(bw, DC_L_CODES, AC_L_CODES)
        emit_zero_block(bw, DC_C_CODES, AC_C_CODES)  # Cb
        emit_zero_block(bw, DC_C_CODES, AC_C_CODES)  # Cr
    bw.byte_align()
    return bw.get()


def build_jpeg(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    sizes = [(8, 8), (8, 16), (16, 8), (16, 16), (24, 16), (16, 24)]
    width, height = rnd.choice(sizes)
    samp_420 = rnd.choice([False, True, False])

    out = bytearray()
    out += MARK['SOI']
    xden = rnd.randint(72, 300)
    yden = rnd.randint(72, 300)
    out += make_app0_jfif(xden, yden)

    def scale_qt(qt: List[int], scale: int) -> List[int]:
        return [max(1, min(255, (q * scale + 50) // 100)) for q in qt]

    scale_l = rnd.randint(70, 120)
    scale_c = rnd.randint(70, 140)
    ql = scale_qt(STD_LUMA_QT, scale_l)
    qc = scale_qt(STD_CHROMA_QT, scale_c)

    out += make_dqt(ql, 0)
    out += make_dqt(qc, 1)
    out += make_sof0(width, height, samp_420)

    out += make_dht(STD_DC_L_BITS, STD_DC_L_VALS, tc=0, th=0)
    out += make_dht(STD_AC_L_BITS, STD_AC_L_VALS, tc=1, th=0)
    out += make_dht(STD_DC_C_BITS, STD_DC_C_VALS, tc=0, th=1)
    out += make_dht(STD_AC_C_BITS, STD_AC_C_VALS, tc=1, th=1)

    out += make_sos()
    out += make_entropy_data(width, height, samp_420)
    out += MARK['EOI']

    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    data = build_jpeg(seed)
    return data[:4096]

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs used by the ProcessStats fuzzer stub.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME will read from this buffer.
# We craft a sequence of strings and integers that exercise:
# - up to 3 map counter entries (keys <=32 chars, vals <1000)
# - a plausible filename
# - an optional debug_output string (<=128 chars)
# - random seeding for coverage while keeping values valid/interesting
#
# Buffer format (custom, self-delimiting for the fuzz harness):
# We encode a sequence of length-prefixed blobs so both FUZZ_PARAM_STR and
# FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME can consume reasonable data slices.
#
# Layout (conceptual):
#  [magic]\n
#  n_entries (1 byte 0..3)
#  for i in [0..n_entries):
#    key_i (len-prefixed string)
#    val_i (uint32 little-endian; we choose 0..999)
#  filename (len-prefixed string)
#  dbg_flag (1 byte 0/1)
#  if dbg_flag==1:
#    dbg_seed (len-prefixed string)
#  trailer padding of some random printable data to allow extra FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls.
#
# Length-prefixed string encoding:
#   uint16 little-endian length L, followed by L bytes.
#
# All strings are UTF-8-ish ASCII content with occasional binary to broaden coverage,
# but the harness accepts arbitrary bytes as text.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,:/\\+@#%[](){}$!~"

def _rand_str(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, allow_binary: bool = True) -> bytes:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Build mostly printable, inject a few binary bytes if allowed.
    s = bytearray()
    for i in range(L):
        if allow_binary and rng.random() < 0.08:
            s.append(rng.randrange(0, 256))
        else:
            s.append(ord(rng.choice(PRINTABLE)))
    return bytes(s)

def _lp(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # uint16 length prefix
    L = min(len(data), 65535)
    return struct.pack('<H', L) + data[:L]

def _rand_key(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Keys truncated to 32 by fuzzer; produce varied lengths up to 48 to test truncation paths.
    # Include duplicates occasionally.
    choices: List[bytes] = [
        b"q", b"quality", b"passes", b"iterations", b"opt_level",
        b"butteraugli", b"dct", b"chroma", b"subsamp", b"meta",
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = rng.choice(choices)
        extra = _rand_str(rng, 0, 24, allow_binary=False)
        key = (base + b"_" + extra)[:48]
    else:
        key = _rand_str(rng, 1, 48, allow_binary=True)
    return key

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Provide common image extensions, nested dirs, and relative/absolute forms.
    exts = [b".jpg", b".jpeg", b".JPG", b".bin", b".dat"]
    dirs = [b"/tmp/", b"./", b"../", b"/var/tmp/", b"C:/temp/", b"/dev/shm/"]
    name = _rand_str(rng, 3, 12, allow_binary=False)
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        ext = rng.choice(exts)
    else:
        ext = b""
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        prefix = rng.choice(dirs)
    else:
        prefix = b""
    # Occasionally include spaces or special chars
    mid = b"" if rng.random() < 0.7 else b" " + _rand_str(rng, 1, 6, allow_binary=False)
    return prefix + name + mid + ext

def _bounded_uint32(rng: random.Random, max_inclusive: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(0, max_inclusive)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = bytearray()

    # Magic to help distinguish our framing in case the harness scans.
    magic = b"GZSTATS\x00"
    out += magic

    # Number of counter entries 0..3
    n = _bounded_uint32(rng, 3)
    out.append(n & 0xFF)

    # Emit entries
    seen_keys = set()
    for i in range(n):
        # Duplicate key sometimes
        if i > 0 and rng.random() < 0.25 and seen_keys:
            key = rng.choice(list(seen_keys))
        else:
            key = _rand_key(rng)
            seen_keys.add(key)
        val = _bounded_uint32(rng, 999)
        out += _lp(rng, key)
        out += struct.pack('<I', val)

    # Filename
    filename = _rand_filename(rng)
    out += _lp(rng, filename)

    # Debug flag
    dbg_flag = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else 0
    out.append(dbg_flag)

    if dbg_flag:
        # Debug seed limited to <=128 by stub; we generate up to 160 to test truncation.
        dbg = _rand_str(rng, 0, 160, allow_binary=True)
        out += _lp(rng, dbg)

    # Trailer: additional len-prefixed strings to satisfy extra FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
    # Provide a small variety of sizes and contents, including empty strings.
    extra_count = rng.randint(2, 6)
    out.append(extra_count & 0xFF)
    for _ in range(extra_count):
        allow_bin = rng.random() < 0.3
        s = _rand_str(rng, 0, 64, allow_binary=allow_bin)
        out += _lp(rng, s)

    # Ensure size cap
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE])
    return bytes(out)

import random

# Generator for valid/interesting JPEG bitstreams to feed guetzli::Process via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME contents.
# Aim: produce mostly valid small JPEGs with varied properties, occasionally minimal headers, to exercise success paths.

# Minimal JPEG building utilities (baseline, no fancy features). Keep under 4096 bytes.

def _be16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>H', x & 0xFFFF)

# Standard JFIF APP0 segment
def _app0_jfif(version=(1,1), density=(72,72), units=1) -> bytes:
    ident = b"JFIF\x00"
    ver = bytes([version[0], version[1]])
    xden, yden = density
    thumb = (0, 0)
    payload = ident + ver + bytes([units]) + _be16(xden) + _be16(yden) + bytes([thumb[0], thumb[1]])
    return b"\xFF\xE0" + _be16(len(payload) + 2) + payload

# DQT for one table (8-bit precision)
_ZZ = [
 0, 1, 5, 6,14,15,27,28,
 2, 4, 7,13,16,26,29,42,
 3, 8,12,17,25,30,41,43,

10,19,23,32,39,45,52,54,
20,22,33,38,46,51,55,60,
21,34,37,47,50,56,59,61,
35,36,48,49,57,58,62,63]

def _dqt(table_id: int, q: List[int]) -> bytes:
    # q is 64-length list in natural order; JPEG DQT expects zigzag order
    zz = bytes(q[i] for i in _ZZ)
    pq_tq = table_id & 0x0F  # 8-bit precision
    payload = bytes([pq_tq]) + zz
    return b"\xFF\xDB" + _be16(len(payload) + 2) + payload

# SOF0 (baseline DCT) for 3 components (Y Cb Cr), with sampling factors selectable
def _sof0(w: int, h: int, samp: tuple) -> bytes:
    # samp: ((Hy,Hv),(Cu,Cv),(Ku,Kv)) factors in [1..4]
    (hy,hv),(cu,cv),(ku,kv) = samp
    precision = 8
    ncomp = 3
    payload = bytes([precision]) + _be16(h) + _be16(w) + bytes([ncomp])
    # Component IDs 1,2,3 with sampling factors and quant table selectors 0/1
    payload += bytes([1, (hy<<4)|hv, 0])
    payload += bytes([2, (cu<<4)|cv, 1])
    payload += bytes([3, (ku<<4)|kv, 1])
    return b"\xFF\xC0" + _be16(len(payload) + 2) + payload

# We'll embed canonical small DC/AC tables that are accepted by most decoders.
# Using common baseline tables (from Annex K) header structure.

# SOS for 3 components using specific Huffman tables
def _sos() -> bytes:
    ncomp = 3
    hdr = bytes([ncomp,
                 1, (0<<4)|0,  # Y uses DC0/AC0
                 2, (1<<4)|1,  # Cb uses DC1/AC1 (we can still provide only table 0 but keep varied)
                 3, (1<<4)|1])
    # Spectral selection and approx for baseline
    hdr += bytes([0, 63, 0])
    return b"\xFF\xDA" + _be16(len(hdr) + 2) + hdr

# Create a simple entropy-coded scan with minimal valid structure: a few 0x00 bytes with byte-stuffing, then EOI.
# While not a real decodeable image, many encoders/decoders accept minimal data; Guetzli's Process typically parses and may reencode.

def _scan_payload(length: int) -> bytes:
    # Avoid marker emulation: stuff 0xFF with 0x00
    data = bytearray()
    for _ in range(length):
        b = 0x00
        data.append(b)
    # Insert some 0xFF to exercise byte-stuffing handling
    for i in range(0, min(8, length), 2):
        if i < len(data):
            data[i] = 0xFF
    stuffed = bytearray()
    for b in data:
        stuffed.append(b)
        if b == 0xFF:
            stuffed.append(0x00)
    return bytes(stuffed)

def _std_luma_quant(quality: int) -> List[int]:
    # Baseline luminance table scaled by quality (simple linear scaling)
    base = [
        16,11,10,16,24,40,51,61,
        12,12,14,19,26,58,60,55,
        14,13,16,24,40,57,69,56,
        14,17,22,29,51,87,80,62,
        18,22,37,56,68,109,103,77,
        24,35,55,64,81,104,113,92,
        49,64,78,87,103,121,120,101,
        72,92,95,98,112,100,103,99]
    qf = max(1, min(100, quality))
    if qf < 50:
        scale = 5000 // qf
    else:
        scale = 200 - 2 * qf
    out = []
    for v in base:
        t = (v * scale + 50) // 100
        out.append(max(1, min(255, t)))
    return out

    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        # 4:4:4
        samp = ((1,1),(1,1),(1,1))
    else:
        # 4:2:0 typical
        samp = ((2,2),(1,1),(1,1))
    # Quality range to vary quant tables
    quality = rnd.randint(40, 95)
    qy = _std_luma_quant(quality)
    qc = _std_chroma_quant(quality)

    # Build markers
    soi = b"\xFF\xD8"
    segs = []
    # Optionally add APP0 JFIF
    if rnd.random() < 0.9:
        units = rnd.choice([0,1,2])
        xden = rnd.choice([72,96,300])
        yden = rnd.choice([72,96,300])
        segs.append(_app0_jfif((1,1), (xden,yden), units))
    # Quant tables: one for Y (id 0), one for CbCr (id 1)
    segs.append(_dqt(0, qy))
    segs.append(_dqt(1, qc))
    # Huffman tables: provide both DC/AC for table 0 and reuse them for chroma too to be simple
    segs.append(_dht_dc(0))
    segs.append(_dht_ac(0))
    # For table index 1, reuse same definitions to satisfy SOS references
    segs.append(_dht_dc(1))
    segs.append(_dht_ac(1))
    # Frame header
    segs.append(_sof0(w, h, samp))
    # Start of scan
    segs.append(_sos())
    # Entropy-coded data payload
    payload_len = rnd.randint(16, 256)
    scan = _scan_payload(payload_len)
    eoi = b"\xFF\xD9"

    jpeg = soi + b"".join(segs) + scan + eoi
    return jpeg

# Additionally, sometimes return raw RGB that begins with SOI to trigger alternate code paths but still valid to parse as JPEG header by heuristics.

def _maybe_minimal(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed ^ 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    # Minimal JPEG-like header only to test error handling that may still succeed sometimes
    soi = b"\xFF\xD8"
    app0 = _app0_jfif()
    # Tiny frame/sos with zero scan to keep very small
    w = 16; h = 16
    segs = [
        _dqt(0, _std_luma_quant(75)),
        _dqt(1, _std_chroma_quant(75)),
        _dht_dc(0), _dht_ac(0), _dht_dc(1), _dht_ac(1),
        _sof0(w,h,((2,2),(1,1),(1,1))),
        _sos(),
    ]
    scan = _scan_payload(rnd.randint(4, 24))
    return soi + app0 + b"".join(segs) + scan + b"\xFF\xD9"

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose among a few constructions
    choice = rnd.random()
    if choice < 0.7:
        data = _build_jpeg(seed)
    else:
        data = _maybe_minimal(seed)
    # Ensure within 4096 bytes
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
